newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER-COLOGNE AND MOENCHENGLADBACH CRASH OUT OF CUP.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-COLOGNE AND MOENCHENGLADBACH CRASH OUT OF CUP.

text.p: Cologne and Borussia Moenchengladbach became the first high-profile casualties of the German Cup on Friday, both dumped out of the tournament in the first round by regional league sides.
Cologne, four-time winners of the Cup, went down 3-1 away to southern German club Ulm.
"Ulm deserved their victory," Cologne coach Peter Neururer conceded. "We're very disappointed. We expect to win a game like this.
"We weren't ready to make challenges and you can't survive against a regional league side like that."
Moenchengladbach's match with Hanover ended 0-0 after 90 minutes and 1-1 after extra time and Hanover keeper Jierg Sievers saved Martin Schneider's spot kick to give his team a 5-3 win on penalties.
Bayern Munich had no such trouble against lower league opposition, thumping village team Waldberg 16-1 away to progress to the next round.
